SELECT a1.Date, a1.Description, a1.Amount, a1.ClientNumber, a1.TranType, a1.LedgerNumber, a1.MembershipID, a1.EFTTransNo, EFTADJUSTMENTLOG.OtherFeesReversed, if(a1.TranType="D", a1.Amount, 0.00) As "Debit", if(a1.TranType="C", a1.Amount, 0.00) As "Credit", a1.Balance, SUM(if(a2.ledgertype = 2, a2.amount, 0.00)) AS "EFTBalance", SUM(if(a2.ledgertype < 2, a2.amount, 0.00)) AS "NonEFTBalance", CONCAT_WS(", ",EMPLOYEES.LastName,EMPLOYEES.FirstName) AS Emp, STORES.StoreLocation, a1.Type, a1.Cleared, a1.LedgerType, a1.SubType FROM accountledger a1 INNER JOIN accountledger a2 ON a1.clientnumber = a2.clientnumber AND a2.DATE <= a1.DATE AND a2.ledgernumber <= a1.ledgernumber LEFT JOIN EMPLOYEES ON a1.EmployeeNumber = EMPLOYEES.EmployeeNumber LEFT JOIN STORES ON a1.StoreCode = STORES.StoreCode LEFT JOIN EFTADJUSTMENTLOG ON a1.EFTTransNo = EFTADJUSTMENTLOG.EFTTransNo and EFTADJUSTMENTLOG.Type="B" WHERE a1.clientnumber = "0000015224" GROUP by a1.ledgernumber ORDER BY a1.ledgernumber DESC;

Subject: 11205 - T-Max / TServer troubleshooting recommendations
Description:
Good afternoon.  Thank you for contacting SunLync Support.  As requested, here are some recommendations for troubleshooting the T-Max / TServer issues.

 

Have a bed technician check the hardware to ensure there are no issues there.

 

Make sure the USB to serial is plugged directly into the computer and not a USB hub.  A USB hub is like a splitter that plugs into one USB port, and provides multiple USB ports.

 

Try a new USB to serial adapter.  We recommend this one:

https://www.amazon.com/Adapter-FT232RL-Chipset-Supports-Windows/dp/B08T92M9KP?th=1

I recommend calling us before attempting to switch it out, as there may be some configuration changes needed to make it work.

 

When the issue does happen and the timer in the room is displaying 0, I recommend checking the T-Max Manager and taking note of what it shows and whether it agrees with the timer in the room or with what SunLync and TServer are reporting.

 

Your case number is #11205.  Please let us know if you have any questions or concerns.

Subject: Canyon Connection Issue
Description:
Hey Brittany,

Here are the steps we discussed today. Try this and call us back if this doesnt work.

**Possible Causes**

1. If you are using a firewall or any kind of web blocker, the connection to Cayan's Site may be compromised.
2. After a Windows update runs and installs updates on the workstation, some Internet Options may need to be adjusted.
3. Cayan's site is down.

**Possible Resolutions**

- Add** **https://ps1.merchantware.net to the **Trusted Sites** on your PC.

1. Click on your start button
2. In the search bar, type "Internet Options"
3. Click on internet options
4. Navigate to the security tab
5. Select **Trusted Sites **icon (Normally represented by a Green checkmark)
6. Click the sites button
7. Type** **https://ps1.merchantware.net in the Add this website to the zone text box then click Add
8.

Click Close when finished



**Lower** Security level for this zone.

-

Set the setting to **Low** by **dragging** the level bar down to the **lowest** setting.



**Adjusting** Advanced Internet options: **Advanced Tab**

- **Look** for and uncheck (if checked) **Check for publisher's certificate revocation.**
- **Look **for and uncheck (if checked) **Check for server certificate revocation.**
- **Look** for and uncheck (if checked) **Check for the signatures on downloaded programs.**
- **Enable Integrated Windows Authentication**.
- **Enable native XMLHTTP support.**
-

Enable TLS 1.2



Open Merchantware backoffice and **test** the connection. If the connection is **not** successful **run** network tests to check the connection to https://ps1.merchantware.net
You can also try **restarting your computer.** Computers restarts can fix common DNS issues which could be preventing the connection to Cayn's site.

_**If the above steps do not work, Contact SunLync support at 866 - SUNLYNC. **_

Description:
No, nothing was set up different on this. The problem is that with SunLync, when a card comes back approved for a partial amount it only allows you to pick from CASH payment types for the remaining balance. And because payment types can't be salon specific it shows them to everyone. There are a couple like this. So when this happens the employee has no choice but to pick one to finalize the transaction. Subject: Voiding from the Floor Plan window
Description:
Hi SunLync Support,

We have had a situation come up more than a few times where an employee voided a tan (that had a fee associated with it) from the floor plan view rather than from the "Misc" menu on the Customer View. Unfortunately, it doesn't refund to the card. We made a video of what happens that you can see on the following link:

https://1drv.ms/v/c/cedd18553ca733e3/EUwe82BCBUJKjc3YbPNM2CwBtJHBM6OaFHtpQITpWgc1JA?e=uGqstg

At about 1:35 into the video, it warns the user that "In order to void only the tan, the client must have only paid with one payment type." In this case, that was true since our test customer only bought a tan and nothing else.

At 1:52 into the video, it warns the user that "Since this is a partial refund..." the funds will not go back on the card automatically. In this case, the one transaction would be the whole transaction. However, the bigger problem we have is employees don't understand what this means since to them "the payment portal" IS SunLync or they don't read the prompts (especially if they made a mistake and need to quickly resolve it).  This has resulted in us not properly refunding a transaction and there being no real way to know what happened. This can make for some pretty upset customers and frustrated staff. So a few questions...


  1.
Is there a way to see a list of transactions that were voided but not refunded to the card, such as a report, that we can monitor?
  2.
Is there a way to disable this option so employees are not permitted to void through the floor plan when money is involved?
  3.
Is there a way for it to actually do a partial refund to the card (such as if I went to "Misc" then "Refund", which allows for a partial refund meaning the logic is in the software and is just not being called from the floor plan interface?
  4.
Is there a way to easily see from the customer's transaction interface when a "void" didn't actually refund to a card? As it is now, a void that refunded to a card looks identical to a void that did.
  5.
Are there other ways to deal with this that might help?

We have tried training the staff, but when it's busy or if an employee is newer, it's easy to forget or overlook. It would be very helpful if the software could help guide them through it with more than a warning. If something isn't clear or you need additional information, please let me know. Any help is appreciated.


Thank you,

Subject: BA 7200 #400 Error Fix
Description:
Hey Chris,

Here are the steps to resolve the #400 error.


1. The error is telling us the control software has a problem.
2. Max tanning time needs to be adjusted using Professional
Manager Setup.
3. Press and hold the minus button until Master-Code 0000 is
showing. Change this to 0001 using the right arrow and + button.
4. You will then see Professional Setup Manger. Press the right
arrow until you see Operation. Press the OK button.
5. You will see a new screen open saying ACTIVATED. Now press
the right arrow once and you will see the Maximum Tanning
Time. Use the + or – buttons to adjust the time to match what is
on the exposure label.
6. Allow the display to return to standby mode.
7. Using the supplied Ergoline tool, gently tighten the door screw
until you can open the rear service door.
8. Turn the internal breaker off for 60 seconds and turn it back
on.
9. Close the rear service door and back the door screw out so it is
secure.
10. Run a full test session to make sure this issue is resolved

Adrian called in regarding an E114 error on their Affinity 500 unit. He stated that the error was previously reported through the unit, and after shutting off the external breaker for a period of time, the unit powered back on a few days later without displaying the error.

Subject: SunLync 10.0.0.7 Issues
Description:
Support,

We have noticed a couple more issues within v10 when freezing a Family Luxury membership, particularly within the affiliated package processes:

POS
When the membership is frozen at POS, the affiliated package remains ACTIVE...which is fine for the current month.

But when the EFT batch posts, it does not put the affiliated package ON HOLD when the customer successfully pays the freeze dues. It leaves the package ACTIVE and the secondaries are allowed to tan illegitimately.


BACKOFFICE
When the membership is frozen in BACK OFFICE, the affiliated package gets set to ON HOLD immediately. The operator then needs to manually reactivate it and set the expiration date to the end of the month or else they cannot tan the remainder of the billing period.

Then the affiliated package expires before the next batch. So when the EFT batch posts, it does not put the affiliated package On Hold and clear the expiration date when the customer successfully pays the freeze dues. It leaves it as expired....THEN when they are reactivated at POS or BACK OFFICE, the affiliated package is correctly put as ACTIVE, but it leaves the expiration date, thus breaking the affiliated package/membership status relationship.

Could we please schedule a time to go through this and show you what we are seeing?

Respectfully,

How do I open and close a cash drawer? 

 

SunLync has a built-in feature to help you count, close, and track cash drawer figures. You may already be familiar with the End of Shift Drawer Count pop-up when closing POS. This is SunLync checking to see if you want to close out and count the cash drawer. 

 

* Count: Use this if you want to count the cash drawer now, at the computer right now. 

* Drop: Drop off the drawer in a safe place like a locked safe to be counted later or take to another computer to count there. 

* Ignore: Keep the drawer open, will close out later. 

 

 

 

Stepping back to the beginning, we must open the drawer. SunLync opens a drawer when completing the first transaction on a new drawer. Based on your SunLync settings, this may happen in the background automatically. To bring this to the front end, log into the Back Office and go to Store Parameters. The Peripherals Settings include controlling how the cash drawer works. Set the default starting cash and checkmark “Prompt for starting cash amount when a drawer is opened”.  

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

SunLync will only show the Starting Cash Drawer Amount pop-up after completing the first sale. Since sometimes there is a gap between putting the cash drawer in and completing the first sale. Processing a $0 transaction, like a tan on an employee’s membership, will ensure the drawer is ready right away. 

 

Along with closing SunLync POS to count or drop a drawer. You can click on Count/Drop at POS to pull up the End of Shift Drawer Count pop-up window. 

 

 

 

 

After selecting Count and the employee doing the count. Enter in the amounts for the payment types completed in the drawer. The numbers will default to $0. 

 

For card and check payment. You may have to run a report in SunLync, your payment provider portal, or print store copies of receipts to put into the cash drawer to get those counts.  

 

When counting the cash, you can use the built in calculator. To count by denominations instead of dollar amounts. 

 

 

 

Next, confirm how much if any cash will be left in the drawer. 

 

 

 

The drawer is now counted and closed. If you use the “Use recommended distribution” setting in Store Parameters, you will see a screen like below instead. Which includes recommendations on what denominations you should leave in the drawer for the next cashier. 

 

 

 

After counting a drawer, you can Edit Amounts if needed. SunLync will track adjustments and flag the drawer as being adjusted and reports. 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

Included with SunLync are the Drawer Figures and Drawer Figures Summary reports. That allows you to easily see the counts and any variances between them.

Subject: T-Max Touch setup
Description:
Good afternoon.  As discussed on our call, here are the instructions for setting up the T-Max Touch:

First, install the drivers as described in this guide:
https://tmaxtimers.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/T-Max-Manager-Touch-USB-Driver-Guide-.pdf
The download link in the guide doesn't appear to work, so here is one that does:
https://tmaxtimers.com/software/T-Max%20Manager%20Touch%20USB%20Driver.exe

Once the drivers are installed, take note of the COM Port number that shows next to the Silicon Labs device in Device Manager.
Then open SunINI on the computer the T-Max is connected to.  If you don't have a desktop shortcut, you can search the start menu:
 ![](https://jkamerica.zendesk.com/attachments/token/9Ecv4JRlvT2Fb6PoGyEKV4rZw/?name=image.png)
You can also access SunINI by clicking the small folder button on the SunLync login prompt:
 ![](https://jkamerica.zendesk.com/attachments/token/ADf5eJcSb5rSyr5PdKT491spd/?name=image.png)

In SunINI, navigate to the Timer Settings page under the Timer Server section.
Change the COM Port number to match what Device Manager shows, then click Save and Close.
 ![](https://jkamerica.zendesk.com/attachments/token/iVqDEx770ZY9IdyUUFezu8YCJ/?name=image.png)

To apply the change, close out of POS and TServer if they are open, then relaunch POS.
To close TServer, first click the small up arrow near the system clock on the right side of the taskbar.
Then right click the icon that looks like a small light blue analog clock, and choose Close.
 ![](https://jkamerica.zendesk.com/attachments/token/oI0ihfId1tYiJPO5BmmWmkYYc/?name=image.png)

Once the changes have been applied, I recommend sending a test to a bed to make sure everything works.  Please let us know if you need further assistance, or if you have any questions or concerns.

Description:
Hello SunLync Support,


I hope you’re doing well.


We’re reaching out because we’ve noticed an issue with how late payments are being processed on memberships that are already scheduled to freeze or cancel.

This has created confusion for both our team and our customers, as we expect the pending freeze or cancellation to remain in place after the late payment is collected.
Could you please explain why this is happening? We’d also like to know if there is a setting or workflow that would prevent a late payment from reactivating the membership and causing an additional monthly draft when the account is already set to freeze or cancel.
We appreciate your help and look forward to your guidance.

Support,

We encountered an issue during the Greenwood Village 8/1 EFT batch submission that we have not seen before.

During the submission, the batch totals went into the negatives, and the logs do not contain the complete batch results. I do not believe "Enable Logging" was enabled for the EFT batch process before the submission, so the attached logs are all that were captured after the issue occurred.

The immediate impact is that approximately 80 transactions remain in an "Open" status. Before we can post the batch, we now have to manually determine which of those transactions were actually processed successfully and update the batch records accordingly. If we do not, we risk submitting duplicate transactions and double-charging clients. The ccprocessinglog shows the few attempts that were made the "Remaining to be billed" value become negative. I'm not sure where the disconnect occurred. The workstation maintained a stable internet connection throughout the process, and I was remotely connected while monitoring the batch and capturing screenshots.

A similar issue also occurred during the Castle Rock batch submission. In that case, I noticed it almost immediately and was able to also capture a screenshot.

At this point, all other batches have been posted without issue. Greenwood Village is the only batch still pending while we wait for guidance.

Could you also advise whether there is an updated version we can install on both the server and workstations so they are running the same build? Currently, the server is running version 10.0.0.7, while the workstations are running version 10.0.0.5.

Our EFT workflow is:

* Batch is created on the server (v10.0.0.7)
* Batch is submitted from an individual store workstation (v10.0.0.5)
* Batch is then posted on the server (v10.0.0.7)

Please let us know how you would like us to proceed with the Greenwood Village batch and whether matching software versions are recommended.

Josh said this is his first time seeing this timer control module, which may explain why the unit was offline. Josh does not currently have a multimeter available to verify voltage at the timer. He will have an electrician check the power coming from the port connected to the timer to confirm it is receiving the proper voltage. If proper voltage is confirmed at the timer connection, a replacement timer may be needed. Provided Josh with the unit schematic and timer reset manual for reference.

Description:
Darrell/6186943272 called in reporting that not all lamps are lighting on his Inspiration 600 unit. He stated that every other lamp on the base was lighting, with the same issue occurring intermittently on the canopy. Incoming power has not been checked recently, but Darrell reported that when it was last tested about a month ago, all three legs were reading 230 volts.
I recommended verifying the incoming power and checking the breakers to ensure no cables are loose, damaged, or burnt. After reseating and turning off the middle internal breaker, Darrell was able to get the base lamps working, leaving only the canopy affected. Since everything else appeared to be in order, I recommended checking the capacitors, as a faulty or burnt capacitor may cause the internal breaker to trip.
I sent Darrell the case number, a photo of the schematic, and a reference photo showing how to access the capacitors on this unit. He will call back after checking the capacitors with his multimeter, which he currently has at another facility.
